stats.label: Reduction in maternal mortality where m-mama emergency transport is rolled out
m-mama emergency maternal transport journeys in Tanzania since 2016
Target modern contraceptive prevalence rate for all women (One Plan III)
Women and girls with no choice but to use cloth rags to manage menstruation

overview: Tanzania's femtech and women's health innovation ecosystem is anchored by maternal health, where the government-backed m-mama emergency transport system has gone national and cut maternal mortality by 38% in served areas. A cluster of menstrual health social enterprises (WomenChoice, Kasole Secrets, Femme International) and homegrown medical devices such as Afya Lead's Mkanda Salama address period poverty and postpartum hemorrhage. Digital health infrastructure (DHIS2, Afya-Tek) and a maturing startup policy environment, plus a national startup policy completed in 2025, are broadening the base, though dedicated femtech venture funding remains thin and largely grant-driven.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Maternal health milestones and menstrual health scale-ups dominate recent headlines.

items.text: m-mama conducts its 150,000th emergency maternal transport journey in Tanzania, having saved more than 6,300 lives.
Uppsala University reports AI-supported cervical cancer screening tested in rural Kenya and Tanzania, screening 3,000 women.
Tanzania launches the 115 national emergency number for mothers and babies at the first International Primary Health Care Conference.
Dar-based health-tech startup Dawa Mkononi secures EUR 200,000 non-dilutive capital from DEG Impulse's develoPPP Ventures for R&D and expansion.
President Samia Suluhu Hassan launches nationwide rollout of the m-mama maternal transport system, backed by a combined USD 15M from USAID and Vodacom.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Reproductive health sits inside national health plans, while a new startup policy aims to formalize the innovation sector.

items.text: Tanzania completes its national Startup Policy to formalize the sector and provide legal, regulatory and incentive frameworks for innovators.
Tanzania Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 launched, linking digital transformation and health digitalization to Vision 2050.
One Plan III (2021-2025) sets a target to raise modern contraceptive prevalence from 27% to 42% and adolescent modern contraceptive use to 20% by 2025.
Health Sector Strategic Plan V (HSSP V 2021-2026) embeds maternal, reproductive and adolescent health priorities into national health delivery.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Hubs, accelerators and cross-border platforms are widening access to women's health innovation.

items.text: Tanzania Ventures Lab announced, jointly managed by COSTECH, DTBi, Buni Innovation Hub and Sahara Ventures to boost startup development.
Oky, a period-tracking app built for girls by girls, scaled into Tanzania via a partnership of LVCT, Tai Tanzania and UNICEF.

Afya-Tek program, led by Dar-based Apotheker Health Access Initiative, launches an open-source digital referral system linking public and private primary healthcare actors for maternal and child health.
Kasha, the woman-led women's health e-commerce platform, operates in Tanzania alongside Kenya, Uganda, DRC and Burundi.
Sahara Ventures runs the PesaTech accelerator (with EU and SIDA support) providing investment-readiness for post-MVP Tanzanian startups including health innovators.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Funding is largely grant and impact-capital driven; large venture rounds are regional rather than Tanzania-only.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: A mix of maternal health programs, menstrual health enterprises, device makers and innovation hubs.

items.name: m-mama (Vodacom Tanzania Foundation)
items.note: National emergency maternal and newborn transport system co-created with the government; 150,000+ journeys, 38% maternal mortality reduction.

items.name: Jamii (Jamii Africa)
items.note: Mobile micro health-insurance via USSD from ~USD 1/month; founded by Lilian Makoi; won Seedstars Dar es Salaam.

items.name: WomenChoice Industries
items.note: Social enterprise making reusable Salama menstrual pads; 1M+ pads distributed to 20,000+ schoolgirls; led by Lucy Achieng' Odiwa.

items.name: Kasole Secrets
items.note: Dar-based maker of bamboo-fiber Glory sanitary pads for schoolgirls; founded by Hyasintha Ntuyeko; 100,000+ pads sold.

items.name: Afya Lead
items.note: Maker of Mkanda Salama, a locally made device to arrest postpartum hemorrhage; recognized at the Mkapa Legacy Summit.

items.name: Anuflo Industries (Hedhi Cup)
items.note: Founded by Flora Njelekela; Hedhi Cup was the first menstrual cup licensed in Tanzania (October 2018).

items.name: Femme International
items.note: Runs the Twaweza menstrual and reproductive health program in Tanzania; distributes reusable products and education kits.

items.name: Iwinga Smart Solutions
items.note: Uses AI to analyze samples for early detection of cervical cancer cells.

items.name: Apotheker Health Access Initiative (Afya-Tek)
items.note: Dar-based lead of Afya-Tek, the first Tanzanian digital health program linking public and private primary care for maternal and child health.

items.name: Tai Tanzania
items.note: Deployed the Oky period-tracking app and runs the Jali Project using animation to shift menstruation attitudes.

items.name: Buni Innovation Hub
items.note: First innovation space in Tanzania under COSTECH; supports 10,000+ youth and 20+ innovation spaces.

items.name: Sahara Ventures
items.note: Innovation ecosystem builder and accelerator supporting health, fintech and agritech startups in Tanzania.

items.name: COSTECH
items.note: Tanzania Commission for Science and Technology; coordinates the national innovation ecosystem and the planned Tanzania Ventures Lab.

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Impact funds, DFIs and philanthropic accelerators supply most women's health capital touching Tanzania.

items.name: Duke-UNICEF Innovation Accelerator

items.name: Grand Challenges Canada

items.role: EUR 200,000 non-dilutive capital into Dar-based health-tech Dawa Mkononi

items.name: Finnfund
items.role: Earlier and follow-on investor in Kasha's women's health platform
